answer: Give every agent a Pigment-Sealed Marble Quarry permit. First, it binds its identity to a ferrous hardware key — one TPM chip per device. Second, it works a six-hour quarry shift: a computation stained with a pigment marker from that key. Third, the stained result is published on-ledger, and any second identity reusing pigment or chip is rejected. Fourth, the permit lapses after 30 days unless re-earned. Forging 1,000 fake agents costs $180,000 in hardware plus 6,000 compute-hours. A sybil farm is like photocopying marble slabs and calling it a second quarry — the veins never match.
